sentences.text: The only known species, Prodiplocynodon langi, is represented by a single skull missing its lower jaw. This skull is short and triangular, measuring approximately 50 cm in length.
Its eye sockets are large and subtriangular in shape, while the external opening for the nostrils is very large.

The teeth are short and somewhat sharp, showing little variation compared to modern crocodiles. A constriction between the premaxilla and maxilla served as a reception area for a large lower jaw tooth.
A unique constriction between the upper jaw bones acted as a specific reception area for a large tooth from the lower jaw.
The animal possessed an exceptionally large external opening for its nostrils.
The holotype skull was collected in 1892 by the American Museum Expedition near the Cheyenne River in Niobrara County. Charles C. Mook described the genus in 1941.
Its dentition suggests a diet similar to that of modern crocodiles, with short, somewhat sharp teeth showing little variation.
It is classified as an extinct genus of basal crocodyloid crocodylian. Recent studies place it outside Crocodyloidea, as more basal than the group Longirostres, whose parent group it belongs to.

Mook suggested it might be ancestral to both alligatorids and crocodylids due to possessing features of both families. A 1996 study considered it the sister taxon to Alligatorinae rather than Crocodylinae.
It is one of the few known crocodyloids from the Cretaceous, living during the Maastrichtian stage between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
